extractedText: Luxury Cars, Luxury Travel NILU: The Analog Hypercar That Takes the V12 Beyond 1,070 Horsepower With a naturally aspirated V12 producing more than 1,070 horsepower, a seven-speed manual transmission, and a cockpit free of central touchscreens, the NILU transforms Sasha Selipanov’s independent vision into a hypercar built around mechanical engagement. Nicolo Di Stefano July 24, 2026 5–8 minutes Automotive Design, Car Design, Hartley Engines, hypercar, Luxury Cars, luxury mobility, Manual Transmission, NILU Hypercar, Nilu27, Sasha Selipanov, supercars, V12 Engine Created by designer Sasha Selipanov, Nilu27’s first automobile combines a naturally aspirated V12 revving to 11,000 rpm, a manual gearbox, and a body shaped around its mechanical architecture. The NILU in motion reveals the philosophy behind Nilu27: a naturally aspirated V12, lightweight engineering, and design shaped by mechanical precision. Every surface, proportion, and movement reflects Sasha Selipanov’s vision of a hypercar created for driver engagement rather than digital intervention. Video courtesy of Nilu27. Used for editorial purposes only. The first ignition of the NILU engine took place on June 17, 2026, in New Zealand. The naturally aspirated 6.5-liter V12, developed with Hartley Engines, produced more than 1,070 horsepower during its initial dyno testing while reaching its intended 11,000 rpm redline. For Nilu27, the young automotive company founded by designer Sasha Selipanov and his wife Inna, the milestone marks the transition from concept to a functioning prototype. NILU enters a segment where performance is increasingly defined by hybrid powertrains, software, and advanced electronic systems. Selipanov chose a different mechanical philosophy: a naturally aspirated engine, rear-wheel drive, and a seven-speed manual transmission with an exposed open-gate shifter. Inside the cockpit, the central touchscreen has been eliminated in favor of analog gauges, physical switches, and controls placed within immediate reach of the driver. Those decisions define the NILU more clearly than its performance figures alone. The car belongs to a small generation of hypercars designed around the physical relationship between driver and machine. The clutch, the movement of the gear lever, engine speed, and steering response all become integral parts of the driving experience. Electronics remain present where necessary without becoming the dominant language of the automobile. From the Bugatti Chiron to an Independent Vision The NILU combines sculpted aerodynamics with a naturally aspirated V12, expressing a design philosophy centered on mechanical purity and driver engagement. Sasha Selipanov has built his career at some of the world’s leading automotive design studios. His experience includes positions within Volkswagen Group, Lamborghini, Bugatti, and Genesis before becoming Head of Design at Koenigsegg. His portfolio includes projects such as the Bugatti Chiron, Lamborghini Huracán, Genesis Essentia, and Koenigsegg Gemera. With Nilu27, Selipanov has been able to create an automobile entirely from his own vision, without adapting it to the design language of an established manufacturer. The name NILU combines the names of the couple’s daughters, Nica and Lucia. The number 27 references one of the most recognizable racing numbers in motorsport history, associated with drivers including Gilles Villeneuve and Jean Alesi. The bodywork reflects that creative freedom. A low front end is framed by large air intakes, while the sweeping windshield wraps around a compact cockpit positioned at the center of the chassis. Sculpted side surfaces rise over the wheels before flowing into a rear section that deliberately exposes the suspension, chassis structure, and mechanical components. The engine becomes the visual centerpiece of the rear design. The twelve cylinders remain partially visible, while three high-mounted exhaust outlets emerge in a triangular arrangement. Rather than concealing the mechanical architecture beneath smooth panels, the design celebrates collectors, suspension arms, structural elements, and engineering details as part of the overall composition. A Naturally Aspirated V12 Designed Without Compromise The 6.5-liter naturally aspirated V12, developed with Hartley Engines, delivers more than 1,070 horsepower and revs to 11,000 rpm, defining the mechanical heart of the NILU. The engine developed by Hartley Engines features an 80-degree, naturally aspirated V12 configuration with a displacement of 6.5 liters. It produces more than 1,070 horsepower at 11,000 rpm and delivers 860 Nm of torque at 7,000 rpm. Nilu27 originally targeted more than 1,000 horsepower, with the first dyno tests already exceeding that objective. The absence of turbochargers defines the engine’s immediate throttle response, sound, and power delivery.
